answers.question: Is it crazy to do one more 16-miler on Wednesday so I feel ready?
answers.answer: It’s better to keep the taper light. A 16‑mile run would add too much volume and likely increase fatigue and heart‑rate drift, which can undo the recovery the body needs right before the race. Stick to the current plan and use the short quality block to build confidence at race pace.

new.analysis:
The athlete asked whether adding another 16‑mile run on Wednesday would help feel ready. During a taper the goal is to keep volume low and maintain a gentle tempo. A 16‑mile session would add significant volume, increase fatigue, and might raise heart‑rate drift, undermining recovery. The athlete’s data show low hard time and good sleep; there is no injury signal, but the additional mileage would not give extra training stimulus when the body needs rest. Instead, keep the current plan and focus on race‑pace confidence in a short quality block. The plan for the following week is a standard taper: one quality session, short easy runs, and rest before the race.

The plan: Monday rest, Tuesday easy 5 mi, Wednesday quality 3 mi with 1 mi at marathon pace, Thursday easy 4 mi, Friday rest, Saturday easy 3 mi, Sunday race.

Key watch items: total mileage, heart‑rate drift, recovery quality, and hydration.

No safety callouts.
